message:
Thanks, I'll help you check. So far I know you live in New Hampshire, your dad (72) lives with you, and you own your home. To narrow down the programmes, please answer these:

1. How many people live in your household, including you and your dad? (1; 2; 3; 4; 5; 6; 7 or more)
2. How many children under 18 live with you? (none; 1; 2; 3; 4 or more)
3. Roughly how much does the household earn from work in a year, before tax? (none; $1 to $10,000; $10,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $30,000; $30,000 to $40,000; $40,000 to $50,000; $50,000 to $60,000; $60,000 to $80,000; $80,000 to $100,000; $100,000 to $150,000; $150,000 or more)
4. How much Social Security does the household get in a year? (none; $1 to $10,000; $10,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $30,000; $30,000 or more)
5. Any other income a year (pensions, unemployment, interest, child support)? (none; $1 to $5,000; $5,000 to $15,000; $15,000 or more)
6. Roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments? (under $2,000; $2,000 to $5,000; $5,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $100,000; $100,000 or more)
7. Does anyone get health insurance through a job? (no; yes)
8. Does anyone have a disability? (no; yes)
reply: Three of us. No, no children. Around 30 thousand a month. Around $2,000 a month. Around $3,500 a month. Somewhere between 25 thousand and 50 thousand. Yes, that's right. No idea, honestly.

message: I want to be sure before I give you an answer, because the amounts make a big difference. Just to confirm: is your household's work income about $30,000 a MONTH (about $360,000 a year)? Your Social Security is about $2,000 a month, and other income is about $3,500 a month? If those are yearly amounts instead, please tell me which ones. Also, is anyone in the household disabled, or getting disability payments? (yes/no/not sure)
reply: Around 30 thousand a month. Around $3,500 a month. Around $2,000 a month. No idea, honestly.

summary: New Hampshire household of 3 (two adults plus a 72-year-old father who lives with them), no children, owns home. Reported household work income is about $30,000 per month (about $360,000 per year), Social Security about $2,000 per month, other income about $3,500 per month, savings and investments $20,000 to $100,000, and someone has job-based health insurance. Income is far above the limits for all ten programmes: SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, EITC, child tax credit, ACA premium tax credit, and free school meals. No programme is recommended. Disability status is unknown, but it would not change the result because income is far too high for SSI or Medicaid. If the income figures were actually yearly amounts rather than monthly, the household should re-screen, since the result could change.
